bodyHtml:
What QUSE actually covered, and where sizing lives now

Short answer: API QUSE was the performance demonstration for crack-height sizing. It qualified a UT examiner to measure the through-wall height of planar cracks that start on the far side, usually the pipe ID, in carbon steel about 0.375 in to 1.0 in thick. QUSE is no longer listed among API's current certifications. Sizing is now part of the QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) exams, which cover detecting, characterising and sizing flaws in carbon steel SMAW butt welds. For turnaround UT sizing, specify QUTE (M) or QUTE (PA). Treat any scope outside that specimen envelope as needing procedure-specific demonstration under ASNT Level III oversight.

A common contract question is: "What flaw types and configurations does QUSE actually cover for piping, and how does that map to the UT sizing work we ask contractors to do during turnarounds?" This section answers it in detail. It uses API's published programme pages (checked October 2026), API's QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) candidate orientation (effective July 2024), and secondary descriptions of the legacy QUSE programme.

Legacy QUSE: scope as it was published

Industry descriptions of the legacy API QUSE (Qualification of Ultrasonic Testing Examiners, Sizing) programme are consistent on its scope:

  • Task: crack-height sizing, meaning the distance from the base of a planar crack to its tip, using equipment and sizing techniques under an API-defined procedure.
  • Flaw configuration: planar cracks starting on the opposite surface from the scanning surface, which for piping means ID-initiated cracks scanned from the OD.
  • Material and thickness: carbon steel, about 0.375 in to 1.0 in thick.
  • Supporting tasks: detecting the flaw, positioning it relative to the weld, and sketching where it sits in the weld.

A phased array version, QUSE-PA, applied the same crack-sizing idea with phased array equipment under its own API-defined procedure. API's current certification list names QUTE (M), QUTE (PA), QUTE-TM and the Long Seam Pipeline programme. It does not list QUSE or QUSE-PA. If a bidder offers a QUSE certificate, check its expiry and its current status with API's ICP directory. Do not assume it can be renewed.

How sizing is assessed in the current QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) exams

API's candidate orientation for QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA), effective July 2024, describes one performance demonstration that combines detection, characterisation and sizing. QUTE (M) uses conventional single- or dual-element equipment. QUTE (PA) uses phased array. The main points, paraphrased:

  • Specimens: carbon steel SMAW butt welds, in flat plate 0.25 in to 1.00 in thick and pipe 2 in to 12 in in diameter, as described on API's QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA) pages.
  • Flaws: weld and base-metal flaws normally associated with carbon steel SMAW welds. Reportable flaws are characterised by type, and cracks are further classed as ID-initiated, OD-initiated, centreline or transverse.
  • Length: reportable flaws are length-sized from start and stop positions. Flaws shorter than 0.250 in may be treated as non-relevant.
  • Crack height: the orientation describes dedicated crack-sizing blocks 0.375 in and 1.00 in thick, where crack height is measured and length is not required.
  • Laminations: base-metal laminations larger than 0.250 in are reported with start, stop and length.
  • False calls count against the candidate, along with missed detections and characterisation errors.
  • Logistics: candidates bring their own instruments, transducers, calibration blocks and procedures. Data are recorded on API-provided electronic forms. The exam runs one 8-hour day at the PRCI Technology Development Center in Houston.
  • Prerequisite: current UT Level II or III, under ASNT employer-based certification or ACCP, an ISO 9712 accredited scheme, CGSB or PCN.

So the ID-crack sizing that QUSE used to cover is now inside QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA), within the same carbon steel, thickness and weld-type limits.

Mapping QUTE to typical turnaround UT sizing scopes

The useful question for a turnaround contract is not "QUTE or Level III?" but "does the QUTE specimen envelope match this inspection task?" The table below is our own engineering mapping. API does not publish it. Use it to decide where a QUTE certificate is relevant evidence and where you need something more specific.

Turnaround UT taskInside the QUTE (M)/(PA) envelope?What to add
Detection and length sizing of fabrication flaws in carbon steel girth welds, about 0.25-1.0 in wall, 2-12 in pipeYes. This is the core specimen set.Site procedure approved by an ASNT Level III, plus a calibration block that matches the job.
Height sizing of ID-connected cracks in carbon steel (for example wet H2S or amine cracking at welds) within that wall rangeLargely yes. Crack-height sizing blocks are part of the exam.A mock-up or procedure demonstration if the crack type, geometry or access differs from the exam.
Walls over 1.0 in, such as heavy-wall vessels, reactors and drumsNo. Outside the specimen thickness.Procedure-specific demonstration on representative blocks. Consider TOFD or PAUT procedures qualified for the thickness.
Austenitic stainless, duplex or dissimilar metal weldsNo. The specimens are carbon steel.Material-specific procedure (often phased array with suitable wedges or dual-matrix probes) demonstrated on matching mock-ups.
Small-bore socket and fillet weldsNo. The specimens are butt welds.Geometry-specific technique, often RT or a specialised UT procedure.
High-temperature hydrogen attack screeningNo.Specialist advanced UT techniques with qualification specific to the mechanism.
Wall thickness at CMLs, corrosion mappingThickness belongs to QUTE-TM, not QUTE (M)/(PA).QUTE-TM where the owner specifies it, or ASNT UT Level II under the written practice. Mapping procedures approved by a Level III.

Two conclusions follow. First, QUTE (M) or (PA) is good evidence for the welds it was designed around, which are a large share of refinery and midstream carbon steel piping. Second, the highest-consequence sizing calls often sit outside that envelope: heavy wall, stainless, dissimilar metal welds, unusual geometry. A QUTE requirement alone does not protect you there. Our pages on phased array inspection and TOFD testing describe the techniques usually used on those scopes.

What API 510 and API 570 say about qualified angle-beam examiners

The in-service codes are the reason QUTE matters to owners at all. API 510 and API 570 use the idea of an industry-qualified UT angle-beam examiner. That means a person with an API ultrasonic angle-beam qualification (historically QUTE and QUSE, now QUTE (M) and (PA)), or an equivalent qualification the owner approves. The codes call for such examiners in specific applications, chiefly where the owner needs angle-beam UT to detect, characterise or size planar flaws, such as ID-breaking cracks examined from the outside. Check the current edition of each code for the exact trigger wording and where it sits in the code, because it has been refined over editions.

Two practical points come out of this. The code requirement is application-specific. It does not say every UT technician on site must be QUTE-certified. And the code allows an owner-approved equivalent. API has also published guidance (API Bulletin 587) to help owners set up in-house qualification programmes equivalent to the API angle-beam qualifications. An owner who cannot find enough QUTE-certified technicians for a turnaround can therefore build or accept an equivalent performance demonstration, provided it is documented and approved before the work.

Where ASNT NDT Level III fits in a turnaround UT clause

ASNT NDT Level III and API QUTE answer different questions. Level III shows that a person can develop, approve and interpret UT procedures, choose techniques and acceptance criteria, and train and examine Level I and II personnel under the employer's written practice to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. QUTE shows that one technician detected, characterised and sized known flaws on blind specimens on one day, with a measured false call rate.

So the direct answer to "do we accept ASNT Level III in lieu of QUTE on UT-related turnaround scopes?" is: not as a like-for-like substitute for the scanning technician on scopes where API 510 or 570 calls for an industry-qualified examiner, unless the owner formally approves an equivalent performance demonstration. Level III belongs in the clause too, as procedure owner and data reviewer. A workable structure:

  • Tier 1, code-triggered planar flaw sizing: technicians hold QUTE (M) or QUTE (PA) for the technique used, or an owner-approved equivalent demonstration on representative specimens.
  • Tier 2, out-of-envelope sizing (heavy wall, stainless, dissimilar metal welds): technique-specific procedure demonstrated on mock-ups and approved by the contractor's ASNT UT Level III, with the owner witnessing.
  • Tier 3, thickness and corrosion mapping: ASNT UT Level II under the written practice, with QUTE-TM where the owner requires it.
  • All tiers: UT procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III holding UT, who also reviews reportable indications before the API inspector acts on them.

Sample clause wording you can adapt

The wording below shows how the tiers can be written into a turnaround NDE contract. It is an example for discussion with your inspection and legal teams, not a code requirement.

  • "Where the Owner's inspection plan requires angle-beam ultrasonic examination to detect, characterise or size planar flaws under API 510 or API 570, examiners shall hold a current API QUTE (M) or QUTE (PA) certification for the technique used, or a qualification the Owner has approved in writing as equivalent before mobilisation."
  • "For examinations outside the QUTE specimen envelope (material, thickness or joint type), the Contractor shall submit a technique-specific procedure approved by its ASNT NDT Level III (UT) and shall demonstrate it on representative specimens, witnessed by the Owner, before production examination."
  • "Thickness measurement and corrosion mapping shall be performed by personnel certified to at least UT Level II under the Contractor's written practice (SNT-TC-1A or CP-189), with API QUTE-TM where specified in the work order."
  • "All reportable indications shall be reviewed by the Contractor's ASNT NDT Level III (UT) before release to the Owner's API inspector, who remains responsible for evaluation and disposition."

Written this way, the clause holds the line on performance demonstration where the code and the consequence call for it. It also gives an approved route when certified technicians are scarce, and it makes clear the Level III's job is oversight and procedure ownership, not substitution.

Verifying UT credentials before mobilisation

  • Check each QUTE, QUTE-TM or legacy certificate against API's ICP directory for status and expiry. API UT certifications run three-year terms with full retesting.
  • Confirm the certificate's technique (manual or phased array) matches the technique the contractor will actually use.
  • Ask for the employer's written practice and each technician's Level II or III certification record, which is also the QUTE prerequisite.
  • Ask which Level III approved each UT procedure, and confirm that person holds UT on their ASNT Level III certificate.
  • For Tier 2 scopes, see the mock-up demonstration record before work starts, not after the first indication is reported.

How Atlantis supports turnaround UT scopes

Atlantis NDT does not deliver API QUTE, QUTE-TM or QUSE training or exams. Our ASNT-certified technicians perform UT thickness surveys, corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD under ASNT Level III oversight, with procedures approved by our Level III. For code-triggered sizing scopes, we staff to the owner's stated qualification requirement. Results go to the owner's API inspector of record. For your own technicians, we train to ASNT SNT-TC-1A: UT Level II training, ASNT certification and Level III training. Send us your turnaround UT scope, ask for a UT procedure review by our Level III, or ask about UT Level II training. We reply with a quote within 24 hours.

More questions on QUTE and QUSE

What is API QUSE?

API's former Qualification of Ultrasonic Testing Examiners (Sizing) performance demonstration, focused on crack-height sizing of far-side (ID) planar cracks in carbon steel. It is no longer listed among API's current certifications. Sizing is now assessed in QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA).

What is API QUTE?

API's hands-on UT performance demonstration family. Currently it consists of QUTE (M) for manual conventional UT and QUTE (PA) for phased array, both for detection, characterisation and sizing in carbon steel SMAW butt welds, plus QUTE-TM for thickness measurement.

Does QUTE cover stainless steel or heavy-wall welds?

No. The published specimens are carbon steel, about 0.25 in to 1.00 in plate and 2 in to 12 in pipe. Other materials and thicknesses need procedure-specific demonstration.

Can an ASNT Level III replace a QUTE-certified technician?

Not automatically. Level III certifies knowledge and procedure authority, not blind-specimen scanning performance. The owner may approve an equivalent performance demonstration under API 510 or 570.
